Ground-truth IBD from a run's tree sequence

Source: R/ibd.R
ibd_pairs.Rd

Computes genome-wide identity-by-descent (shared-segment length / sequence length) among a set of genomes, keyed by pedigree id, from the tskit tree sequence recorded by the model.

Usage

ibd_pairs(run, ids = NULL, pairs = NULL, min_span = 1000, segments = FALSE)

Arguments

run

a run: a vivax_run (from run_sim() or load_run()) or the path of a run directory.

ids

the pedigree ids of the genomes to compare, every pair among them; NULL for every genome the tree sequence records, which warns when that is more than 1e6 pairs.

pairs

instead of ids, a data frame of pairs to compare, with the pedigree ids in columns a and b: only these pairs are computed, about 0.2 ms each, so use it for a few pairs among many genomes, such as each recurrence against its host's earlier episodes.

min_span

the shortest segment returned, in bp, after the cut at the junctions: a segment of exactly min_span is kept. It does not change ibd.

segments

if TRUE, also return every shared segment with its common ancestor and that ancestor's age.

Value

a vivax_ibd object, a list of:

  • pairs, a data.table keyed by a and b: one row for every pair of distinct genomes found, a < b (integer pedigree ids), and ibd (double, in [0, 1]), 0 for a pair that shares nothing;

  • samples, one row per genome found, by pedigree id: pedigree_id, node_time (ticks before the end of the run) and tick (the day the genome arose, as in events.tsv);

  • missing, the requested ids the tree sequence does not hold;

  • segments, NULL or a data.table, by pair and position: a, b, chrom (the PvP01 chromosome), start and end (bp within the chromosome, end exclusive), gstart and gend (bp along the concatenated genome), length (bp), mrca_id (the pedigree id of the common ancestor), mrca_time and depth (its age, see Segment ages);

  • sequence_length, min_span, all_pairs (TRUE: every pair of the genomes is in pairs; FALSE for listed pairs, which hold each listed pair of two distinct genomes found, once, with a < b), end_tick (the run's last tick) and trees (the file read).

Read a pair's value with ibd_lookup(), or the table with as.matrix() or as.data.frame().

What is counted

A pair's ibd counts all shared ancestry: every stretch over which the two genomes descend from a common ancestor genome, of any age and any length, over the sequence length. min_span does not change it. To impose a cutoff, ask for segments and filter them on their length or their age (see Segment ages).

Segments

A segment is a maximal stretch over which two genomes descend from one common ancestor genome, cut at each chromosome junction: a change of ancestor starts a new segment even with no gap between them. A pair gets the same segments whatever other genomes are passed, the same as ibd_segments() gives, and at min_span = 0 they add up to its ibd.

Ids that are not in the tree sequence

In a run written with RETAIN_FULL_HISTORY = FALSE, most genomes not alive at its end leave the tree sequence. A requested id it does not hold is listed in missing, gives one warning, and looks up as NA, not as 0; asking only for such ids is an error.

Segment ages

mrca_time is a tskit node time, ticks before the end of the run, not an age. A segment's depth is how long before the older of the two genomes its common ancestor lived, mrca_time - max(node_time[a], node_time[b]), in ticks. A recency filter is written against it, for example x$segments[depth <= 180] for ancestry within about six months: filtering on mrca_time alone scores a pair by when its ancestry last branched, not by how related the two genomes are.

Cost

segments = TRUE takes a few times as long and gives one row per segment per pair, so restrict it with ids and min_span.

Python

The IBD and ARG functions read a run's tree sequence with Python's tskit, through the reticulate package. Either of two routes works. Automatic: with no Python chosen, reticulate sets up its own environment with tskit (>= 1.0) and numpy the first time one of these functions runs; this needs internet once. Your own Python: set RETICULATE_PYTHON to a Python that has those modules (in ~/.Renviron to keep it) before the first such call of a session. A function that cannot reach them stops with an error of class malariafwd_no_python that says what to do, and check_setup() reports what is found.

See also

ibd_lookup(), ibd_segments()

Examples

run <- example_run()
x <- ibd_pairs(run, ids = classify_cases(run)$pedigree_id[1:30])
x
#> <vivax_ibd> 30 genomes, 435 pairs, min_span 1000 bp
#>   segments: not computed
#>   from /tmp/RtmpUQ7ECQ/malariafwd-example-run-60b2e786/plasmo.trees, ending on tick 400
as.matrix(x)[1:4, 1:4]
#>     51 82 98 121
#> 51   1  0  0   1
#> 82   0  1  0   0
#> 98   0  0  1   0
#> 121  1  0  0   1
